messages.subject: Calculating detection probability in MCDS
parts:
Hello Distance list serve-
I have questions on how to calculate the probability of detection in MCDS=
. There=E2=80=99s an older post relating to Distance 5, and I see that t=
he example in Distance 6 v2 is a corrected example using the Amakihi data=
set. I=E2=80=99ve managed to reproduce detection probability curve from =
the Distance output of the user manual=E2=80=99s Amakihi example (with co=
rrections=E2=80=94see below), but this example does not include a covaria=
te=E2=80=A6.a similar Amakihi example in Marques et al.=E2=80=99s 2007 Au=
k manuscript demonstrates this sort of output with a MCDS model, but the =
covariates are a factor and a continuous, and so Distance automatically p=
rovides the factor-only output. So, my first problem relates to my inabi=
lity to duplicate the results of the Amakihi example on p. 99 of the Dist=
ance 6 v2 user=E2=80=99s guide (=E2=80=98Calculating probability of detec=
tion=E2=80=99). In the =E2=80=98key(10)=E2=80=99 section, I think the 35=
.36 is a typo and should read 35.46 (this is parameter A(1), p. 97). For=
the =E2=80=98series(10/82.5)=E2=80=99 calculation, I obtain 0.12233 inst=
ead of 0.1581, and for =E2=80=98series(0/82.5)=E2=80=99 I obtain 0.1497 i=
nstead of 0.199. These discrepancies make very little difference in the =
overall result--g(10) using =E2=80=98my=E2=80=99 values is 0.9379, while =
on p. 99 g(10) is 0.928, rounded to 0.93). But I=E2=80=99ve successfully=
reproduced the curve in the output of the model in the Amakihi dataset, =
which makes me think that there may be some small problems with the numbe=
r crunching on p.99=E2=80=A6.or? My second question relates to applying =
this to my scenario. I want to derive probabilities at levels of one fac=
tor covariate while controlling for levels of another factor covariate. =
My most highly-supported model (half-normal key with 2-term cosine adjust=
ment) includes a covariate for sex (3 levels; female, male, and unknown g=
ender) and site (4 sites). I would like to calculate the detection proba=
bility for each level of sex while controlling for site (i.e., =E2=80=98a=
verage=E2=80=99 the sex-specific detection function across study sites). =
To do this, I multiplied each site coefficient by .33 in the detection p=
robability formula. Here=E2=80=99s an example of how I applied this appr=
oach to calculate s (scale parameter) in the half-normal key series:
88.46 * exp(-.66 + (.33)(-.19)+(.33)(.03)+(.33)(-.25)),
Where 88.46 is the intercept of the scale parameter, -.66 is the coeffici=
ent for females, and -.19, .03, and -.25 are the coefficients for sites 1=
, 2, and 3, respectively. I used this value (39.97) as the value in the =
key series expansion. I have made a plug-and-chug formula in excel that =
satisfactorily (seemingly) creates sex-specific curves =E2=80=98averaged=E2=
=80=99 by site. Does this approach seem reasonable? Thanks for insights=
on both the example in the user=E2=80=99s manual and about my applicatio=
n. My email is druth...@usgs.gov; I=E2=80=99m happy to summarize and r=
e-post whatever advice I find. Cheers, Dan
